newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir says Bakun delay due to technical hitches.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir says Bakun delay due to technical hitches.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Tuesday that technical hitches had delayed the signing of the Bakun dam's construction contract.
"I am told it is some technical hitches .... still some arguments over who is responsible for what between developer and contractor," he told reporters at an energy conference.
He denied that internal squabbles between the various shareholders, as reported in the Asian Wall Street Journal on Monday, was holding up the contract signing.
"The Asian Wall Street Journal report seems to know better than the shareholders. There's no internal squabbles, not that I know of," Mahathir said said.

The dam's main contractor, Ekran Bhd said late on Monday that the 13.6 billion ringgit contract, awarded to a consortium led by Asea Brown Boveri ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG, would be signed sometime in October.
Ekran did not give further details in a statement issued to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange accompanying its annual results for the year ended June 30.
Mahathir did not comment about speculation that the signing ceremony may have been put off due to the ill health of Ekran executive chairman Ting Pek Khiing.
Ting was in Singapore's Mount Elizabeth Hospital September 19-28, though sources at hospital would not disclose the reason for his stay.

The signing ceremony was supposed to be held on Monday but was abruptly postponed without explanation late on Friday -- the second time this month the ceremony was scrubbed -- leading to stock market speculation that Ting was in ill health.
Minister of Energy, Post and Telecommunications Leo Moggie told reporters on Monday the delay was because parties to the contract were still haggling over the fine print.
"I believe the legal people and the contractors want to finalise the wordings of the agreement...," he said.
Officials at Ekran have declined to comment on the postponements.

The agreement was to be signed between the dam's operating company Bakun Hydroelectric Corporation (BHC) and the ABB consortium whose other major partner is Brazil's Companhia Brasileria Projectos e Obras (CBPO).

The consortium in June was awarded the contract to design and build the dam, located in the remote interior of Malaysia's Borneo state of Sarawak. Work on the 2,400MW dam was scheduled to begin in January and completed by 2003.

The BHC groups Ekran Berhad, the Sarawak State Government, the Sarawak Electricity Supply Corporation, the national electricity company Tenaga Nasional Bhd, the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) and Malaysia Mining Corporation.
